“I Looked East and I Looked West” from Taxi Mauve

This from Taxi Mauve, I’m not sure how to add stocatto to the notes, but in measures 3 and 4, the second and fourth notes get bit off short, as if you were saying “do it, do it, do it, do it”. Same in the B part, but not as pronounced. This in the A part is a nice figure that sets the character of the tune when played like this.

X: 1
T: I Looked East And I Looked West
M: 2/4
L: 1/8
R: Polka
K: Gmaj
GB B/c/B/A/|FAA B/A/|GABc|^cd=cA|
GB B/c/B/A/|FA A3/2B/|cAFA|FGGB:|
dg f/g/f/e/|fA A3/2B/|cdef|fg f/g/f/e/|
dg f/g/f/e/|fA A3/2B/|cAFA|FGG2:|

as an alternative, 2nd measure as |FAD B/A/| and 6th measure as |FAD A/B/|. These add a really nice bop to the flow, and actually increase the speed possible on a mandolin.

↳ Posted by justjim on December 1st, 2007.

I Looked East And I Looked West/Paddy Scanlon’s

Paddy Scanlon was a flute player in the parish of Glin (Limerick) with whom Martin Mulvihill played frequently in his youth, and it was from Scanlon that he learned this polka (sleeve notes).

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on June 16th, 2013.

I’d also picked this up, among versions, from another Limerick flute player, John Joe Harnett, who, with everything else, had a load of polkas and slides traditional to the area…

↳ Posted by ceolachan on June 16th, 2013.
